digest.headline: Kubernetes v1.37 and AI Tooling Updates
digest.intro: This week brought several significant platform stability updates from Kubernetes, alongside new capabilities in AI model tooling. Teams are gaining better control over resource scaling and storage management.

items.title: Kubernetes v1.37: etcd RangeStream Cuts Memory Use
items.summary: etcd RangeStream graduates to beta in Kubernetes v1.37, reducing memory usage for large collection reads.
items.whyItMatters: Teams can make peak memory usage more predictable when reading large resource collections.
items.action: Relevant if you manage large Kubernetes clusters.

items.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Storage Version Migration Enabled by Default
items.summary: Storage Version Migration (SVM) is now General Availability in Kubernetes v1.37 and enabled by default.
items.whyItMatters: Teams can ensure consistency when interacting with object storage and API resources.
items.action: Relevant if you use object storage with Kubernetes.

items.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Scale Workloads to Zero with HPA
items.summary: Kubernetes v1.37 introduces Beta support for HorizontalPodAutoscaler scaling workloads down to zero replicas.
items.whyItMatters: Teams can save resources by removing the last idle Pod from queue consumers and batch processors.
items.action: Relevant if you manage queue consumers or batch jobs.

items.title: Playco cuts manual fixes 50% prototyping games with GPT-6 Astra
items.summary: Playco used GPT-6 Astra to build game prototypes, reporting 50% fewer manual fixes than before.
items.whyItMatters: AI models can significantly accelerate the rapid prototyping phase of game development.

items.title: Ollama's transparent pricing
items.summary: Ollama's Pro, Max, and Team plans now use industry-standard per-token pricing with usage included.
items.whyItMatters: Teams can better budget and track usage when running AI models via Ollama.

sources.summary: Using GPT-6 Astra, Playco built three themed game prototypes from one grey box foundation and reported 50% fewer manual fixes than with the previous model.

sources.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Scale Workloads to Zero with HorizontalPodAutoscaler
sources.summary: Kubernetes v1.37 includes API support for horizontal autoscaling of workloads down to zero replicas. This feature is now Beta and enabled by default. A HorizontalPodAutoscaler (HPA) that uses a suitable object metric or external metric can now scale a workload to zero replicas, then bring it back when the metric changes. Before v1.37, you needed an add-on or external component, or you had to enable the Alpha feature gate, to scale from zero. It is now part of core Kubernetes. Scaling to zero removes the last idle Pod from workloads such as queue consumers and batch processors. The savings...

sources.title: Kubernetes v1.37: etcd RangeStream Cuts Memory Use on Large List Reads
sources.summary: I am excited to announce that etcd RangeStream is graduating to beta in Kubernetes v1.37. Paired with etcd v3.7, it reduces the memory the API server and etcd need to read a large collection, and makes peak usage more predictable. The cost of large readsThe API server serves most list and watch requests from its in-memory watch cache. Populating that cache requires reading a resource's full state from etcd, at startup and on every re-initialization. For a resource with many objects, or large ones, such as Pods, that read is expensive. The API server already paginated these reads, asking...

sources.title: Kubernetes v1.37: Storage Version Migration Enabled by Default
sources.summary: I am excited that storage version migration (SVM) has graduated to General Availability (GA) in Kubernetes v1.37! After a number of releases of work and testing, the built-in StorageVersionMigration API (storagemigration.k8s.io/v1) and control plane controller are now fully stable and enabled by default across all v1.37 Kubernetes clusters.
